project_description_summary.value: Design-Build project at Norfolk Naval Shipyard to repair and stabilize soil erosion on the earthen berms surrounding three 120-foot diameter, 2-million-gallon above-ground concrete fire protection water storage tanks (constructed 1940s, buried by earthen berm). Scope includes: (1) mechanically stabilized slope repair of failed berm areas using specialty geotechnical contractor; (2) engineered slope surface treatment and erosion mitigation; (3) security fencing replacement; (4) option to relocate existing overhead electrical lines underground. Triggered by record rainfall in 2016 causing rills, gullies, and localized slope failures along Tanks 553 and 555.
project_description_summary.quote: The project Repair Soil Erosion at Reservoir Berms will design, permit, repair, and construct using innovative mechanically slope stabilization methodologies of the existing berm around the water reservoir tanks. Due to record heavy rainfall events in 2016 and the steepness of the existing berm, the berm and slopes have experienced, rills, gullies, and localized slope failures.

taxonomy_notes.bfa_role_notes: BFA authored the electrical narrative and electrical BOD. On a NAVFAC Design-Build, BFA appears to be acting as the electrical subconsultant to a Design-Build prime (the electrical documents are BFA-authored design deliverables for the contractor's DOR package). Flagged for human review — could also be prime_consultant if BFA held the prime A-E subcontract. Source documents do not explicitly name the prime contractor.
taxonomy_notes.award_type_notes: Design-Build with best-value evaluation language in RFP (technical + price tradeoff). Marked best_value. Could also be qualifications_based if Brooks Act applies to the A-E component, but the prime here is a design-builder, so best_value is more accurate.
